top_evidence.document_title: Thoracic endovascular aortic repair for retrograde type a intramural hematoma or aortic dissection with intimal disruption in the descending aorta: Systematic review and meta-analysis
top_evidence.text: The selection of articles adhered to stringent inclusion criteria, encompassing original studies reporting the short-term or long-term outcomes of the use of TEVAR for RTAAD or RTAIMH. Exclusion criteria included review articles, case reports, and investigations involving animal subjects. Additionally, studies not documented in the English language were excluded from consideration.

top_evidence.text: Funnel plots were generated to assess data symmetry regarding post-TEVAR aortic dimension measurement changes (remodeling) (Figure 6). The funnel plot analysis yielded no signi fi cant evidence of publication bias for the examined postoperative factors ( p > .1). The symmetric distribution of the data points suggests that there is no evidence of selective reporting, indicating that the included studies encompass a representative range of outcomes.

top_evidence.text: The author(s) declared the following potential con fl icts of interest with respect to the research, authorship, and/ or publication of this article: A thorough literature search was conducted using the electronic databases MEDLINE and EMBASE up to April 2024. The search strategy incorporated the following keywords: ( ' type A aortic dissection ' OR ' TAAD ' OR ' type A intramural hematoma ' OR ' type A IMH ' ) AND ( ' endovascular ' OR ' stent graft ' ) AND ( ' retrograde ' OR ' retrograde extension ' ). Two reviewers (N.N. and H.T.) independently carried out the search to identify relevant articles.

top_evidence.document_title: Thoracic endovascular aortic repair for retrograde type a intramural hematoma or aortic dissection with intimal disruption in the descending aorta: Systematic review and meta-analysis
top_evidence.text: The initial screening of articles was executed based on titles and abstracts, with potentially pertinent articles proceeding to a comprehensive full-text review. Subsequently, two reviewers (N.N. and H.T.) independently evaluated the full-text articles for eligibility, resolving any discrepancies through discussion and consensus. Data extraction was independently performed by the two reviewers, utilizing a standardized data extraction form. The extracted information from each included study included the author ' s name, year of publication, study design, sample size, characteristics of the study population, perioperative data (such as operation time, short-term mortality, spinal cord injury, stroke, new intimal tear or dissection in the ascending aorta, and aortic rupture), as well as rates of aortic re-intervention and mortality. Any discrepancies in data extraction were resolved through discussion and consensus.
